summary: The party retested the fused lantern-staff and confirmed that the same incantation blinds anyone who looks at it, while Ord sees the Ethereal Plane and the spirits clinging to Sylan. When Sylan took the staff, a black pillar pulled all six into him. Walker returned from a brief meeting with Vecna: they share interests rather than a clear bargain, Vecna wants his sister-skin book back, and the golden eagle he tapped on the war table lights the map and is only half of a pair whose match Walker believes sits in Vecna’s palace in Nyx. Dana pressed the white helm Walker wears as a possible phylactery. They agreed not to destroy one until they have eyes on its owner, and the group split: Dana, Walker, Ord, and Ciri went to Carlkin’s lighthouse with Elrus, Araden, and Glimmen, while Sylan and Gerk stayed to deal with the spirits. Inside his sword, Sylan met a raven emissary who named him Raven’s razor, told him he had already sent the six on, and stopped him from pulling them back. In New Navel, Sheriff Haldor banned extradimensional and interdimensional doors and spirit-taking inside the city, identified one of the dead as Ledzbika, and explained the town’s returned dead as celestial echoes rather than ordinary ghosts. At the lighthouse, Carlkin’s soul-detecting bag only smoldered, and a soul identifier showed the helm is not a phylactery but carries a tiny soul-memory of the emperor Walker killed. Walker has a slight, not-yet-parasitic link from speaking with that imprint, put the helm back on, and suggested using the fragment to track the emperor.

plotSections.title: Fused lantern-staff
bullets: Sylan and Ord retested the fused lantern-staff with the same incantation. It reproducibly blinds people who look at it. Sylan avoided the effect by not looking. Gerk was blinded again while off to the side, could not say whether he had looked, and treats it as a repeat of an earlier blinding.

The fused item has an evocation aura. While the blinding incantation is active, Ord sees the Ethereal Plane in grayscale, including the spirits attached to Sylan. Sylan could also see those spirits once he took the staff.

plotSections.title: Spirits drawn into Sylan
bullets: When Sylan grabbed the staff to help Ord, a black pillar shot up and the spirits were pulled into Sylan, not into the staff. All six are with him again.

The party will not describe them beyond this: they seem to be people of New Navel, with gripes against some people there and possible unfinished business. Sylan suspects the fused item splits by user — a blinding effect for Ord, and spirit-gathering tied to his own darker inclination. He thinks he might be able to speak with the six in his own realm, and he is not sure they can actually be conversed with.

plotSections.title: Walker returns and the evening plan
bullets: Sylan wants the group to plan the next decision and may go to New Navel to pursue the spirits' unfinished business. Gerk does not want to be cursed and does not want to join a ghost investigation. Sylan calls him a strong Karnak Mar after fumbling an orc term.

Walker flies back in. Sylan asks if he is alive and still their friend; Walker answers, "Why wouldn't I be here?" Sylan asks for a report and whether Walker ran into mind-control trouble. Walker brushes that aside and points at Sylan's magical darkness and soul-sucking as the larger explanation owed.

Sylan proposes a ghost investigation tonight and saving Walker's leads for later. Dana, Walker, and Ciri agree; Ciri is in because of the soul-sucking. Walker had planned to tell the story over dinner, and Sylan is fine waiting because it is still early.
Walker checks that everyone is present. Sylan thinks Ciri is hiding in a tree and possibly blinded; she is standing directly behind him. The DM confirms the whole party is there.

plotSections.title: Vecna, the sister-skin book, and the golden eagle
bullets: Walker reports a short meeting with Vecna at the old training grounds. He downplays any deal: they have common interests, not a clear bargain. Vecna wants his sister-skin book back. Walker says Vecna tried to pass the book off as rat skin when it is his dead sister's skin. Sylan asks whether her soul might still be in it; that is not answered.

Dana asks whether Vecna at least hinted at the phylactery. Walker says the hint, in hindsight, was Vecna tapping a golden eagle on the table; at the time Walker thought Vecna was bored. Walker now has the eagle. Set on the war-table map, it lights the map. He thinks this piece is only half of a pair, and that the counterpart is in Nyx at the palace Vecna was using, the headquarters with the big red wall. Putting this piece on that table is the lead he has.

The party cannot name that capital. Walker appeals to Sylan as being from there. Walker, Sylan, and Gerk throw out several garbled candidates and drop it. The transcript had cut off once as Walker started to elaborate on the book.
Sylan asks whether they picked up the "seasman" and whether the party already went back. Dana says the "season" was shattered, in pieces on the floor.

plotSections.title: The helm as a suspect phylactery
bullets: Dana argues the helm is the only piece of his armor still left, and that it matches her vision of an ordinary item that would pass under their noses. She suspects they have been carrying the phylactery because Walker liked the hat. Walker says he grabbed it, that it is extraordinary, and that it sits over his nose, not under it. He doubts a mundane-looking worn object is the phylactery.

Sylan says they need to examine it, and that if Walker will not allow that he will treat the helm as something hindering him. Walker asks if that is a threat. Dana says no threat is needed: nobody has actually looked at it, and they only need to rule it out. Ciri steps behind Walker and whispers that they are only threatening a good time.

Dana says identifying it would take detect magic and arcane investigation. Ord offers to detect magic. Sylan adds that Carlkin already said he could identify the helm if they brought it, and that Walker can have it back. Dana says Carlkin was worried Walker had been carrying it this whole time: Carlkin has contacted them twice from wherever he is, Walker has had the helm the whole time, and he has not had the eagle the whole time. She notes a phylactery is usually imagined as a treasury object, not something worn, which is why this one would be missed.

Walker still doubts it and agrees they can check, but he will not give the helm to the party. He will hand it only to Carlkin. Sylan asks whether the helm benefits Walker; that goes unanswered. While Sylan broods, the wind carries dark leaves and the weather is abnormally cold for the season. Sylan asks how close Glimmen is, and the scene cuts off as Ord starts to respond.

plotSections.title: Glimmen and the helm
bullets: Dana asks Glimmen in Draconic whether Walker has changed in any odd way since he started wearing the helm, wanting a sanity check from the mind link. Walker says that if Grixto is influencing either of them, it would be Glimmen.

Glimmen clamps her mouth around Walker's head by the helm, which hurts her, lifts him by it, and tells him through the link to give up the helmet. He refuses and says he will hand it only to Carlkin. She rests her head on him and asks whether phylacteries are flame resistant, offering to torch the helm. Walker says not necessarily and tells her not to.

Glimmen says Walker seems influenced, that she is unfit to diagnose it, and that his internal fire can spread and protect her through their bond. In Draconic she tells Dana he has not acted any stranger than normal. She still wants to light him on fire to see if it burns, and says he will be fine. Walker says he is fire resistant and does not think he is fireproof. Ciri starts a tinderbox under his arm.

plotSections.title: Do not destroy it early
bullets: Sylan says that if the helm is the phylactery they should not destroy it immediately. They should find him first, because if he senses the phylactery destroyed he can make another before they have him. Walker agrees they should destroy it only when they have eyes on him. Sylan says they can still rule the helm out.
Sylan offers a same-day appointment with Carlkin if Walker will not take the helm off in front of the party.

plotSections.title: Who goes to Carlkin
bullets: Gerk says not to walk in on Carlkin because he is in a bad way. Ord agrees he is not available. Sylan says Gerk should skip that visit and that he probably should too. Dana says both of them should stay home.

Sylan proposes that he and Gerk handle a separate errand, heard as Ghost Cop and Skeptic Cob, while the others talk to Carlkin. Ord asks how Gerk is supposed to be bad cop if he cannot threaten anyone. Dana agrees, on the conditions of no doors to nothing dimensions, no abyssal monsters, and no opening doors in moving vehicles.

Sylan tells Walker that Gerk's door training has improved and that he can manipulate doors a little better, but still needs work. He sets a regroup at dinner in the castle to plan the next step, does not wait for objections, and tells Gerk it is time to talk to ghosts.

plotSections.title: Elrus offers to train Gerk
bullets: Elrus hears that Gerk needs training and says that makes two of them. He is willing to train Gerk, tells Walker to have the helm investigated, and says Walker's training can resume afterward. He walks up and pokes Gerk in the midriff.
Elrus looks vaguely half-elf and stands about 5'10" to 5'11". He also has an ancient copper-colored dragon. Gerk already knew about the dragon and did not know this height.

Elrus says Gerk is strong of body and lacking in mind, and that they will work that out of him. He calls it no insult: one does not insult an oak as a sapling, knowing it will be more. The growth he means is in the mind. He says Walker needs help meditating and asks whether Gerk has meditated. Gerk asks Ord if he is being insulted. Ord tells him that at least he is strong of body. Gerk does not want to get bigger, because he barely fits places as he is.

Dana explains meditation as being quiet in the mind, like the focus Gerk uses to open a door, because otherwise doors open into the abyss and giant monsters come out. Gerk says that happens only when he thinks about nothing. Dana says they still need his rage, channeled appropriately, and that the doors are a separate kind of focus. Gerk thinks raging while opening a door would go poorly. On the seventeen-foot door he only tried to open it harder. Sylan suggests he try it at the next training. Gerk says maybe.

plotSections.title: Warning Carlkin and the split
bullets: Morning in the forest, after the party spent the morning sorting out where people had been. The DM recap flags that Walker may have made a deal with Vecna, and that a sister-skin journal is involved and is concerning.

Sylan, heading toward New Navel, asks Dana to notify Carlkin that they are returning today, because they are not within five hundred feet. Walker asks why they cannot just walk in. Sylan says last time they had no appointment, barged in, opened a portal to the abyss, and he broke Carlkin's floor, so Carlkin wants warning. Dana agrees, and says they are lucky he allowed another appointment; she had thought he might tell them never to speak to him again.

Sylan warns that Carlkin may be wildly hung over and suggests a snack and maybe a lesser restoration, which Ord might perform. Dana says they will figure it out on arrival. She Sends that they are heading that way and are not bringing Gerk or Sylan. Carlkin has an opening, and the Carlkin group needs to leave now.

The lighthouse group is Dana, Walker, Ord, and Ciri, with Elrus and Araden following; Glimmen goes with them. Walker is going with that group and is not flying off. Sylan and Gerk stay behind, then go to New Navel, and regroup at dinner in the castle. Ord and Ciri need rides; Dana's broom cannot take passengers. Araden carries Ord and tells him his wings are in his chest. Sylan asks Ciri if she wants a door, and she says there is a welcome in there.

plotSections.title: The fused lantern changes hands
bullets: Sylan borrows the fused lantern-staff from Ord so they can see whether a different wielder changes the effect. Ord agrees to tell him the activation wording. The exact word is not spoken. Taking it does nothing catastrophic.
Sylan plans to take the item to Shades and Trades and have it identified in its fused state, unless that was already done.

Sylan wishes he could still use a greatsword while holding the lantern. He has no tail and does not want one. He has heard of a reincarnation spell that left people with tails, and says his appearance has already changed from one experience.

Before going down the vale, Sylan wants to check a place his sword can take him, where he can see spirits like the ones they are after. If those spirits are there, he means to get them out, because it is not a good place to be, and he does not think people would want to see that in the open. Gerk does not like the ghosts. Sylan says he will defend him.

plotSections.title: Sylan's sword and Raven's Razor
bullets: Sylan enters his sword before New Navel and becomes ghostly and translucent. Gerk's rocks fall through him and pile at his feet; Gerk outlines his feet in stones. To Gerk he looks foggy while he is gone.

The sword opens on a rolling gray field, emptier than on earlier visits. The DM briefly calls it the abyssal plane, then corrects that it is not that place. Sylan confirms he released the giant and does not believe anyone is still held inside. A few figures are visible in the distance.
He prays and tries to draw those six figures to him. Arcana 21. The grass at his feet darkens and he feels fishing-line pulls as he reels them in. He registers four beings in sight and six pulls.

A raven drops out of a flicker in the gray sky, hovers two or three feet from his face, and meets his nod by looking him over. It becomes a feather-draped, anemic-looking, middle-aged person built somewhere between a halfling and a dwarf, either a thin dwarf or a very muscular halfling. The figure calls him Razor and Raven's razor, says the spirits were not attached to him, that he already sent them on, and asks why he is pulling them back.

Sylan releases the pull. He is told he is the pathway to the falls and that a razor of the Raven Queen must seek out those who — the rest is lost when the mic cuts. He hears enough to feel the role is clearer, thanks the figure, and agrees not to pull more spirits back. They had unfinished business, but he says it is time they move on. The figure answers that they did, but she will say.

He leaves the gray place and finds Gerk's rocks piled around his feet, the largest about pumpkin-sized. He calls the work a ghost-cop routine and does not want the others there any time soon, though he allows that Gerk might come some other time.

plotSections.title: Spirits of New Navel
bullets: Sylan tells Gerk the ghost-cop plan is smaller than expected. He believes that the last time he walked through New Navel, including on the way to Carlkin's, he inadvertently picked up spirits. Nearness finishes them: they are drawn into him like air into a flame. He is unsure whether the trigger is a touch, their time being up, or their having been truly bad, and he says you cannot cheat her in the end.

He frames the duty as moving people on at the end of their allotment. The ones he must hunt cling out of greed or jealousy of life, often undead or bodiless spirits. He is not sure what to do with spirits who are not bad, and he will not force anyone. He recalls six souls by description only, with no names, and will describe them to the sheriff rather than dig through notes.

He asks Gerk to find the sheriff — he does not remember a mayor, and jokes that the party might as well be one and that they are not that responsible — and to put out word that any spirit willing to move on should find Sylan. If the mayor is a spirit, Gerk should do the talking.

Sylan stays outside town so he does not collect more spirits. Shades and Trades sits in the middle of town. He now thinks its proprietor was a ghost, and he has been near that proprietor before without taking him.

plotSections.title: Carlkin's lighthouse
bullets: Gerk goes into town for the sheriff. The others fly to Carlkin's lighthouse. Glimmen and Araden land in and beside the streets. Araden, the larger copper, tucks her wings and keeps her tail off the roofs, then sets Elrus down.

Dana knocks as the point person. After a crate, a chain, and metal on metal, Carlkin the tortle opens and checks that Sylan and Gerk — and their portals — are not with them. Dana confirms they are absent and that there are no portals or shenanigans.

Carlkin recognizes the second dragon as the copper Araden, not Glimmen. Dana explains that Walker has been training with an established dragon rider and that this dragon is his mentor's. Benji, a warforged, pushes past Dana; Araden perks up. Elrus and Benji embrace. Benji says Elrus looks old for his age and asks about longer meditation. Elrus has been training his new recruit and calls Walker over to meet him. Dana says the party already met Benji in The Reach, including during the Sunder Chase, though Walker had not introduced them. The DM notes Elrus and Araden had not previously interacted with Benji.

Carlkin and Benji date their friendship to around the start of the Sunder Chase and dispute who gave whom the idea. Another copper dragon is still around and is now a hoard dragon for that race. Riding Araden would now count as cheating and get a rider disqualified; she also simply flies faster than a typical ship. Carlkin calls the Sunder Chase a death race.

The party won the Sunder Chase with guidance Carlkin takes some credit for. He singles out Ord for dispelling magic on another ship, a use of that talent he says has not been seen in generations. Most competitors rely on cannons, faster sails, or burning ships; a dragon simply outflying a ship is the other counter. Ord says someone else would have thought of the dispel eventually.

plotSections.title: The white helm
bullets: Dana raises the ornamental, hobgoblin-inspired white helm Walker apprehended and is wearing. Carlkin still treats a lich phylactery as the likely reading. Walker says it is not one and that it is very mundane. Walker hands it over.

Carlkin's belt pouch opens to about two feet across. He dunks the helm in and snaps it shut. He enchanted the bag of holding to detect soul magic of the kind acquainted with a phylactery and to burst into flames on contact. Nothing happens at first, and he says it can be returned in ten to fifteen minutes.

Dana asks about the little eagle. Walker rolls a 27 Perception and sees the pouch's bottom-right corner smolder. The bag does not flash into flame. Carlkin tears it off his belt and it smolders across its surface like slow-burning moss. He says a phylactery would have been a full fire; this slow burn means trace soul magic and maybe further enchantments. He accuses Walker of having understated it. Ciri whispers that it looks like a phylactery. Carlkin says it is not a full phylactery and that it does not look like an ordinary helm.

Walker, who is fire resistant and has his golden glove, reaches into the burning bag. The damage is negligible after resistance. The interior is only large enough for the helm and a little extra. The bag's bottom burns through, and the rest fractures like over-tapped crystal and blows away burning. He is left with a slightly smoking white helm, cool to the touch, taken from the Emperor.
Carlkin invites him inside to identify what he has been wearing. Walker stays. Dana goes in out of curiosity, and Ciri follows to needle Walker.

plotSections.title: Carlkin's study
bullets: Dana, Ciri, and Ord follow Walker into Carlkin's study. Elrus, Araden, and Benji stay outside and talk.
The floor is still a mess from the day before: flagstones in the center are torn up, as if someone had heaved a sandbox out of the floor.
Carlkin has Walker set the helm on a small altar-like lectern at his corner desk and starts going through papers. Dana's question about the little eagle is not answered before the scene cuts away.

plotSections.title: Finding Sheriff Haldor
bullets: Gerk is alone in New Navel looking for the sheriff. In the market he asks a living vendor, who sends him southwest past the tavern to Haldor's house.

He pays her one gold for a small wicker chicken and refuses a life-size wicker goose, saying he has to kill geese on sight as a religious matter and calling them little demon birds. A vendor two doors down sells only geese, caged. Gerk points at him and says he will be back.
Haldor is on his porch in a rocking chair, boots on a stump, hat brim low. He already knows Gerk, has not seen him in quite some time, notices him coming, and agrees to walk out and talk to Sylan.

plotSections.title: The spirit jug, the file, and the door ban
bullets: Gerk says Sylan sent him: bad spirits are flying into Sylan like a jug, and they need help sending those spirits on. They settle on a spirit jug as the picture — spirits go into Sylan so they can be sent home. Haldor knows Sylan as the short elven friend with the sword that only looks large, treats the spirit-taking as new, and checks that none of the party has been taken in. Sylan is just outside the gate.

Gerk is carrying the wicker chicken. He warns that he threatened the goose vendor, mostly in jest. Haldor knows that vendor as a decent man with a caged flock and tells Gerk not to threaten villagers. Haldor also says he and Gerk both know Gator can be difficult; it is unclear whether Gator is that vendor.

Haldor drops a cutpurse to deal with the spirit-sucking. He already has Carlkin's report from yesterday: an extradimensional door in the commons, which he calls a hell portal and a tentacle-spewing portal, plus the floor repair. Extradimensional doors are not allowed inside the city. Gerk says his other doors had been interdimensional and that he did not know this one would be extradimensional.

Carlkin also filed charges Haldor has not sorted out. Haldor keeps one file on the whole party under the label stronghold hooligans, most of it from Carlkin, and would rather wait for them to leave than walk to the stronghold and do the paperwork. His ordinary work is catching cutpurses. Gerk says they will apologize and expects Carlkin to yell.

On the walk, Haldor writes into his notepad that extradimensional and interdimensional doors are now both prohibited inside the city limits, that magic practice belongs in the forest, and that taking spirits in is also not permitted. He hopes Gerk has interdimensional shackles. Gerk does not, offers to open a doorway to fetch some, and is told not to.

plotSections.title: The Trigash beacon
bullets: Walking out, Gerk recaps the day: after Carlkin they practiced doors in the woods, away from people, then Sylan had them try the fused lantern-staff. Sylan blinded Gerk. While Gerk was blinded, spirits went into Sylan, said they wanted to go home, and said there are bad spirits in town that also need sending on.

Haldor places that earlier the same day, around midmorning, in Trigash Forest, a couple of miles off. A giant beacon came out of the sky. He bet Erwin twenty-five gold that it was a random event; Erwin said it was the stronghold hooligans. Haldor now owes the money.
Erwin saw a bunch of them fly that way with a new dragon in tow. About an hour later they flew back out. The fliers reached town a good forty-five minutes before this talk. Gerk and Sylan walked.

plotSections.title: Six New Navel dead and Ledzbika
bullets: Haldor greets Sylan with a handshake, calls him under the weather, and repeats the spirit-jar version. Sylan says he is a cleric of the Raven Queen, one of her servants, tasked with finding people who escaped their end. He thinks he gathered six townsfolk by accident and has no names. Ord was working the lantern in the forest; the big light was that. The party can already see spirits, but the lantern let Ord see the ones following Sylan, and sending them on was the duty.

Sylan recounts the spirits they dealt with: one hostile figure disliked the party and wanted to give something back to Sylan; a woman was frightened, wanted help, and did not want to go back; after they were struck they became partly tangible and started changing. The one he remembers most clearly at first is an older humanoid woman, a grandmother type, and he asks whether she might already have died.

Haldor knows nothing of gods, has had no recent missing-persons reports, and says an old humanoid woman is not enough to identify anyone. Sylan then remembers an elderly high elf man, Ledzbika, who named his neighbor Claire Belle, and a name like Hofford that is only half-remembered.

Haldor knows Ledzbika as an elderly man who died about a month ago of natural causes and often ranted that his neighbor was stealing from him. Claire Belle was trying to steal his belongings. Ledzbika did not come back as a ghost, which Haldor calls the puzzle. In the last six or seven months the town has had a handful of deaths, maybe as many as a dozen, plus uncounted travelers. He calls New Navel a frontier town.

plotSections.title: Echoes, the lantern, and leaving
bullets: Haldor says the town's returned dead are echoes, celestial copies of who they were, and that echoes, undead, and spirits are different, with spirits falling under undead. A portal into another dimension fits these spirits not being in a corporeal form. Sylan agrees they were not corporeal. Summoning undead is against town rules. Haldor tells them to keep the lantern hidden or he will confiscate it. Sylan agrees to keep it wrapped.

When the place was still Neville, residents and travelers escaped without realizing it was a prison of sorts. Those who died could die normally or return as a celestial echo of themselves. Haldor only half-remembers the cause: an elder god tied to the sea, and some consequence of using that being. He says that arrangement is why the city is not full of undead. Ledzbika staying dead is the exception he cannot explain.

Sylan asks whether these celestials came from New Navel, then weighs two worries: that he has failed his duty to find lost souls, or that New Navel traps souls. He sets that aside for lack of time, decides the celestials are not part of what he is dealing with now, and may look into them later. Haldor says the mines across the lake are reopening, competition is up, and all sorts of people are passing through.

Haldor wants to know how long they will stay. Sylan says they will have dinner, make plans, and leave soon on a mission; he cannot say exactly when and does not expect them to linger. Haldor says nothing new has come up and that Gerk can explain. He asks them to keep Gerk's dragon friend away from the ghosts, forbids opening doorways into the tavern or elsewhere, says friends may open ordinary doors and they should just walk in, and tells them to keep the commotion outside town. Gerk answers that he will use only windows. Haldor refuses that, says he does not have the paperwork, and walks back to the porch.

plotSections.title: Town errands
bullets: Gerk shows Sylan the wicker chicken he bought for one gold. Sylan thinks it is well made. Gerk says it also has uses and, asked whether he killed them, says not yet. Sylan offers to buy the geese instead.

Sylan starts toward Shades and Trades the long way to be sure he did not miss anyone. Gerk says Haldor told him to stay out of town and that Carlkin wants them arrested. Sylan jokes that court is politics, but slower, and walks off. The table pauses that scene and returns to Carlkin's lighthouse.

plotSections.title: The helm is soul-bound, not a phylactery
bullets: Carlkin has been measuring the helm and taking notes. He grinds reagents in a mortar and pestle, mixes them with a brackish, pond-water-like liquid, and shakes a two-to-three-ounce vial until it turns crystal clear. He calls the result a soul identifier, akin to the bag test but meant to read the item more closely. He says it is definitely not a phylactery: a phylactery would have burst into flames and might have provoked a stronger magical reaction.

A drop placed on the helm does not run off. It pools and sticks where it lands. Through a magnifying glass, Carlkin finds a spiritual attachment and asks whether Walker interacted with it spiritually when he picked it up.

Walker confirms that after he killed the emperor he spoke with him through the helm. The talk was calm and respectful. The emperor was a hobgoblin in purple robes, different from before, called Walker's golden fire his life force, and wants people to rule as they did before the Voyager gods. Carlkin calls it spooky and asks if Dana has heard this.

Carlkin checks Walker's left arm, cough, and pulse. The helm carries a soul memory. The lich died wearing it, leaving a tiny fragment of being, memory, or imprint. That imprint burned Carlkin's bag, but slowly. Walker has a slight, not-yet-parasitic link from having interacted with the bound soul, and is not highly possessed. Walker puts the helm back on.

Carlkin warns that queasiness, numb earlobes, a tingling left armpit, or voices other than Walker's own, his inner voice, or Glimmen would mean the possession is taking hold. Keep the helm from light-domain clerics of high regard and from feeble-minded wearers. Gerk must never put it on.
Walker suggests using the fragment like an address to track the emperor, and looks for a soul-worker he thinks came with them. Sylan is not there. The scene cuts off as that is being clarified.

log: Sylan reports that another try of the lantern and staff fused them, and says the group should know their abilities before a fight. The party retests the fused lantern-staff. The same incantation blinds onlookers again, including Gerk. Dana notes the blinding. Sylan is unaffected because he does not look, and he asks whether Ord and Gerk were looking.
Gerk says he was away from them doing his own thing, is unsure whether he looked, feels victimized, and wants compensation.

Ord says he used the same incantation, that the blinding is reproducible, that the item has an evocation aura, and that during the blindness he saw a grayscale view of the Ethereal Plane with spirits attached to Sylan.

Sylan says those spirits seem to be people of New Navel with unfinished business, and that the party will not describe them further. He sees them after grabbing the staff. A black pillar shoots up and all six spirits are sucked into him.

Sylan suggests Ord keeps a blinding use and that he himself gathers spirits. He may try to speak with them in his realm, and he may follow their gripes to New Navel. Ord calls it possible unfinished business, and the party agrees to follow that lead.
Sylan proposes the group plan their next move, using the orc term Karnak Mar for Gerk. Gerk refuses to be cursed or to play ghost investigator.

Walker flies back in. Asked if he is alive and still their friend, he says he is here. Everyone is confirmed present. Ciri is behind Sylan, not hidden in a tree. Sylan asks how the trip went and whether mind control was a problem. Walker deflects toward Sylan's darkness and soul-sucking.
The party agrees to a ghost investigation tonight and to take Walker's lead afterward, with the debrief able to wait for dinner. Walker reports now instead of waiting.

Walker says he met Vecna at the old training grounds. They may share interests rather than a firm deal, including recovering Vecna's sister-skin book. Vecna wants the book back and tried to pass it off as rat skin. Walker identifies that skin as his dead sister's, and Sylan asks if her soul is still in it.

Walker places the golden eagle Vecna was tapping on the war table, and the map lights. He believes it is half of a pair and that the counterpart is at Vecna's palace in the capital of Nyx, the headquarters with the big red wall, which nobody can name. He identifies the tapping as the phylactery hint he missed in the moment.

Sylan recalls something previously collected, which he calls the seasman, being picked up and the party going back to it. Dana says the season was shattered in pieces on the floor. Walker is cut off while beginning to describe the book.

Dana asks whether Walker made a deal with the god of the undead and whether that being hinted at the phylactery. She presses the helm as the possible phylactery: the last piece of his armor, her vision of an ordinary item under the nose, and two remote contacts while Walker had the helm but not the eagle. Walker rejects the mundane reading and agrees they can still check it. The party recalls that Carlkin offered to identify the helm and was already worried Walker was wearing it. Sylan insists on an examination and moves closer. Dana and Ciri lower the temperature. Ord offers detect magic.
Sylan broods in an unseasonably cold wind and asks how close Glimmen is.

Dana asks Glimmen in Draconic whether the helm has changed Walker. Glimmen seizes the helm in her mouth, tells Walker to give it up, says he has not acted any stranger than normal, and later offers to burn it to test whether it is a phylactery.
Walker refuses to surrender the helm to anyone but Carlkin. He says he is fire resistant, not fireproof. Ciri starts a tinderbox under his arm.
Sylan and Walker agree not to destroy a confirmed phylactery until they have eyes on its owner, because he could make another. They still intend to rule the helm out and have Carlkin examine it.

Gerk says Carlkin is in a bad way. Dana decides Gerk and Sylan should stay away from that visit. Sylan sends them on a separate errand and tells the others to see Carlkin. Dana forbids doors to nothing dimensions, abyssal monsters, abyss doors, and doors opened in moving vehicles. Ord questions how Gerk can be bad cop if he cannot threaten anyone.
Sylan reports that Gerk can manipulate doors a little better and still needs practice. Elrus offers to train Gerk's mind and to resume Walker's meditation training after the helm is investigated.
Elrus, vaguely half-elf and about 5'10" to 5'11", with an ancient copper dragon, tells Gerk he is an oak sapling who is strong of body and weak of mind. He says Walker needs help meditating.
Dana separates rage from the focus used to open doors. Gerk says the seventeen-foot door was him trying to open it harder, not raging. Sylan suggests he try raging at the next training.

Sylan asks Dana to warn Carlkin before they return to New Navel. They are outside sending range, and last time an unannounced visit opened a portal to the abyss and Sylan broke the floor. Dana agrees to Send that the group is coming and that Gerk and Sylan are not with them. She had thought Carlkin might refuse them forever. Sylan warns that Carlkin may be hung over and suggests a snack or lesser restoration.

The split is set. Dana, Walker, Ord, and Ciri go to Carlkin's lighthouse. Elrus follows with Araden on that side, and Walker is not flying off on his own. Sylan offers Ciri a door. Dana says Carlkin has an opening and that group needs to go. Sylan and Gerk split off to deal with ghosts. The party agrees to regroup at dinner in the castle.

Sylan takes the fused lantern-staff from Ord to test another wielder and, if needed, to identify it at Shades and Trades. The command phrase is not given. Grabbing it has no immediate effect. He then leaves with Gerk.
Sylan says his sword takes him to a bad place where he can see spirits and pull them out if they are there. He will check it here before going down the vale to New Navel.

It is morning. Both groups leave the forest. The DM notes Barker may have dealt with Vecna, and a sister-skin journal. Walker, Ciri, and the others fly toward Carlkin's lighthouse. Sylan and Gerk remain for the spirit-realm check, then New Navel.
Dana's broom cannot take a passenger. Araden carries Ord and Ciri and tells Ord his wings are in his chest. Elrus follows with Araden.
Sylan enters the sword and turns translucent. Gerk tries to stack rocks on him. They fall through, and Gerk traces rock boots around his feet.

Inside the sword, Sylan finds a mostly empty gray field. He confirms the giant was released and does not think anyone remains inside. Distant figures are still visible. He prays and, with Arcana 21, tries to summon the six figures. The grass darkens and the pulls come in like lines on a fishing line.

A raven swoops to face him, acknowledges his nod, and turns into a short, broad, middle-aged, feather-draped person between halfling and dwarf. The figure says the spirits were not attached and that Sylan had already sent them on, then asks why he is pulling them back.

The figure calls Sylan Raven's razor and the pathway to the falls and starts to define whom he must seek. The instruction to seek out "those who…" is cut off. What comes through afterward sounds like "look for the math." The figure stops him from pulling the spirits back.

Sylan releases the spirits. They had unfinished business; the figure says they did, but she will say. Sylan thanks the figure, agrees not to pull more souls back, and leaves. He reappears with rocks piled on his feet. Gerk has been collecting rocks and says Sylan looked foggy. Sylan declines to share the experience and says there is little adventure in the ghost-cop work.

Sylan tells Gerk he likely picked up the spirits by walking through town on the way to Carlkin's, and that being close is enough for them to be drawn into him like air into a flame. He recalls six souls by description rather than name, remembers no mayor, and asks Gerk to find the sheriff, or the mayor if that is who watches the town, and announce that willing spirits should come to him. He will wait outside town. He first plans to approach Shades and Trades while he reconciles which dead he should take, then decides to avoid Shades and Trades for now.
Gerk heads into the city. The others fly to Carlkin's lighthouse. Glimmen and Araden land, and Araden lets Elrus down at the door.

Dana knocks. Carlkin confirms Sylan and Gerk are absent, then recognizes Araden as a copper dragon distinct from Glimmen. Benji greets Araden, embraces Elrus, and Elrus introduces Walker as his new recruit. Dana introduces herself and recalls meeting Benji in The Reach during the Sunder Chase. Carlkin identifies Benji as a warforged.

Carlkin and Benji tie their history to the start of the Sunder Chase, including another copper who is now a hoard dragon for the race. Carlkin credits the party's victory and Ord's dispel on a rival ship, and treats riding Araden in the race as grounds for disqualification.

Carlkin asks why the party is back. Dana raises the helm Walker apprehended. Carlkin identifies it as the one on Walker's head and treats it as a likely lich phylactery. Walker says he does not think it is. Carlkin calls it ornamental and hobgoblin-inspired and asks to inspect it. Walker takes off the white helm and hands it over.

Carlkin drops the helm into a belt pouch that opens to about two feet across. He explains it is a bag of holding enchanted to detect phylactery soul-magic and burn on contact. He says a phylactery would have triggered it, hesitates, and says he does not think this is one. He tells Walker he can have it back in ten to fifteen minutes.

Dana starts to ask about the little eagle. Walker's 27 perception catches the bottom right of the pouch smoldering. Carlkin rips the bag off his belt. It smolders across the whole bag instead of bursting into flame. He reads that as trace soul magic and possibly more enchantments, not a full phylactery, and says they must wait until the bag burns away.

Walker reaches into the burning bag with his golden glove. The heat is negligible because of his fire resistance. He recovers the helm. The interior was only large enough for the helm and a little extra. The bottom burns through, and the rest fractures like tapped crystal and blows away burning.

Carlkin calls it a slightly smoking white helm taken from the Emperor, cool to the touch, and invites Walker into the lighthouse to learn what he has been wearing. Dana, Ciri, and Ord go in with them. Elrus, Araden, and Benji remain outside and talk.
Carlkin's study is still wrecked a day on, with upheaved flagstones in the center. He has Walker place the helm on a small altar-like lectern and looks through papers.

The scene cuts to Gerk, alone, searching New Navel for the sheriff. In the market he asks a living vendor rather than a ghost. She says the sheriff may be at the tavern or at his house, and directs Gerk southwest: past the tavern, down the road, then right. The house is Haldor's.

Gerk pays her a gold and buys her wicker chicken. She also offers a life-size wicker goose. He refuses and says killing geese on sight is religious for him. A goose vendor two doors down reacts, and Gerk tells him he will be back.

Gerk reaches Haldor's house. Haldor sits relaxed on the porch in a rocking chair, boots on a stump, and watches Gerk from under his hat. Gerk waves. Haldor recognizes him and hears that Sylan needs help rounding up bad spirits and sending them home.

Gerk describes spirits flying into Sylan like a jug. Haldor confirms this is new, that none of the party was taken, and agrees to talk to Sylan outside the gate. Gerk mentions Joanna's chicken, his hatred of geese, and a mostly jesting threat against the goose vendor. Haldor tells him not to threaten villagers.

Haldor sets aside a cutpurse and a pentacle-spewing portal in someone's house. He says Carlkin reported an extradimensional door in the commons, which is not permitted in the city, plus a floor repair and charges he has not sorted out. The party shares a sheriff's file labeled stronghold hooligans, mostly Carlkin's complaints, and waiting them out is less paperwork.
Gerk recounts Carlkin, doorway practice in the woods away from people, the hoard lantern-staff, being blinded, and spirits entering Sylan who want to go home, including bad spirits still in town.

Haldor identifies the beacon as Trigash Forest earlier today. He bet Erwin 25 gold that it was a random event rather than hooligans with a new dragon, and lost. Erwin saw the party fly that way with a new dragon and fly back about an hour later. Gerk says he walked. Haldor says the flyers arrived about forty-five minutes ago and the forest is a couple of miles away, then takes Gerk to find Sylan.

Haldor says sucking people up is illegal, asks for interdimensional shackles Gerk does not have, and rejects opening a doorway inside the city to fetch them. He reads a posted change banning extradimensional and interdimensional doors in the city, restricting magic practice to the forest, and banning spirit-taking.

A short walk later, Haldor and Gerk reach Sylan outside the gate. Haldor greets him. Sylan says he serves the Raven Queen, seeks people who escaped their end, and accidentally gathered about six New Navel folk after Ord's lantern revealed the spirits around him. He remembers them mainly as an older humanoid woman. Haldor reports no recent missing persons and asks for a real identifying feature.

Ord recounts a hostile spirit who wanted to give something back to Sylan, and a frightened woman who wanted help and did not want to return. The spirits became partly tangible or started changing when hit. Sylan and Ord identify the elderly high-elf man as Ledzbika. Sylan floats the name Hofford as something he would not remember. Haldor says Ledzbika died of natural causes about a month ago, did not return as a ghost, and had accused his neighbor Claire Belle of trying to steal his things.

Haldor separates celestial echoes from undead and spirits. Summoning undead is illegal, so the lantern must stay hidden or be confiscated. He explains Neville as an unwitting prison whose dead could return as celestial echoes, possibly because of an elder sea god, which is why the city is not full of undead. Recent deaths number a handful to maybe a dozen over six or seven months, including travelers, and he mentions mines reopening across the lake.

Haldor tells Sylan the lakeside mines are reopening and traffic through New Navel is picking up. Sylan sets the celestials aside for lack of time. Haldor asks how long the party will stay. Sylan says dinner, then they plan to leave soon because they are on a mission, and asks if Haldor needs anything. Haldor defers to Gerk.

Haldor warns them off ghosts, forbids doorways, rejects Gerk's windows joke, and tells them to keep the dragon friend away from the ghosts, open no doors in town, and keep commotion outside town. He then returns to his porch.

Gerk shows Sylan the one-gold wicker chicken, says it has uses, and says he has not killed them yet. Sylan compliments it and offers to buy the creatures Gerk has not killed yet. Sylan starts for Shades and Trades the long way. Gerk says Haldor barred him from town and that Carlkin may want them arrested. Sylan jokes about court and walks off.

The scene shifts to Carlkin's lighthouse. Carlkin finishes a clear soul-identifier potion, drips it on the helm, and the drop sticks. He finds spiritual residue and asks about Walker's contact with the emperor. Walker describes a calm talk after killing the purple-robed hobgoblin emperor, who was different: the golden fire as his life force, and rule as it was before the Voyager gods.

After a cough and pulse check, Carlkin tells Dana and Ord that Walker has a slight, non-parasitic connection to a soul memory on the helm. Walker puts the helm back on. Carlkin forbids Gerk from ever wearing it and lists escalation signs and people who must not wear it. He explains the lich died in the helm and left a tiny imprint, which is why the bag burned slowly.
Walker proposes using the fragment to track the emperor and asks after the soul-worker. Sylan is not with them, and the line cuts off.
